instructions: Make these on the weekend: put the 16 corn husks in a large bowl or the sink, cover with hot water, and weigh them down with a plate. Soak for at least 30 minutes, or overnight.
Heat the broiler. Put the poblanos on a baking sheet and broil for 7 minutes, turn them, and broil for 5 minutes more, until charred in spots.
Transfer the poblanos to a bowl and cover it with a plate for 10 minutes. Peel off the skins, remove the stems and seeds, and cut the peppers into 16 long strips.
Cut the cheese into 16 long sticks.
Beat the 3/4 cup shortening in a large bowl with a mixer for 2 minutes, until smooth and creamy.
In a separate bowl, whisk the 2 1/2 cups masa harina, the salt and the baking powder.
Add the dry mix to the shortening a little at a time, alternating with 2 1/4 cups hot water. Beat until you have a smooth, spreadable dough, scraping down the bowl as you go.
Drain the husks and shake off the water. Spread about 2 tablespoons of masa in a thin layer over the wide end of a husk.
Lay a poblano strip and a cheese stick down the middle. Fold in the sides, then fold up the narrow end. Repeat with the rest, standing the tamales open end up.

Put water in the bottom of a large steamer and lay any torn husks there. Stand the tamales upright, packed snugly, and cover. Steam over medium heat for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, checking the water level now and then.
Check one: the masa should pull away from the husk easily. If it hasn't after 2 hours, turn off the heat and leave them covered for 1 hour.
Let the tamales cool completely. Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days, or freeze in a freezer bag for up to 3 months.
To eat them, leave the husks on and steam for 15 to 20 minutes from the fridge, or 30 to 40 minutes from frozen. Or wrap one in a damp paper towel and microwave until hot. Serve with the salsa verde.
advance_prep_notes: make the whole batch ahead (about 3 hours), then refrigerate or freeze; steam to reheat on the morning
method_notes: Lead is In Mama Maggie's Kitchen (4.98 from 45), a 30-tamale batch; here it's cut to 16, which is about 4 per person. Lard is swapped for vegetable shortening and the masa is mixed with hot water, so it stays vegetarian. The page says refrigerate up to 4 days, freeze up to 3 months, and steam to reheat. Other well-known versions (Isabel Eats, Maricruz Avalos, Salt and Wind) were blocked, so there was no second source to compare.
